solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Does polish make such goods better?

definitions.text: Does polish make such goods better?

indicators.note: to make something better is to work on it and change it, so these letters are reworked

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper wonders whether buffing up tarnished stock would improve it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Does' looks like the verb opening a question, but it is part of the letters. Read whole, the clue also describes the answer: polish is just what grubby display stock needs.
explanation.definitionFit: Shop-soiled describes stock that has become dirty or faded from being handled or displayed in a store.

clue.text: Demonstration somewhere in Greater Manchester includes local politician

indicators.note: a place that includes someone has them inside it, so the town wraps the politician

blocks.note: Sale is a town in Greater Manchester
a Member of Parliament represents a local constituency

explanation.surface: A protest in a Manchester suburb draws in the local MP.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Demonstration' suggests a protest march; here it is a sample, a specimen showing what something is like.
explanation.definitionFit: A sample is a small part given to show the quality of the whole, a demonstration of it.

clue.text: Flashy gold kind of string around bronze back

indicators.note: going back means travelling the other way, so the colour word is read right to left

blocks.note: or is gold in heraldry
bronze and tan are both brownish skin colours
the E string is one of the strings of a guitar or violin

explanation.surface: A garish gold string is wrapped around a bronze statue's back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Around' only places the string beside the colour, at the end of the answer, rather than enclosing anything.
explanation.definitionFit: Ornate means elaborately decorated, which comes close to flashy or showy.

clue.text: Relatives get nun at home to cut salad

indicators.note: cutting into something means breaking inside it, so the home word goes into the salad

blocks.note: nuns are addressed as Sister
slaw is coleslaw, a cabbage salad
someone at home is in

explanation.surface: Family members fetch a nun who is home to chop up a salad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut' suggests chopping vegetables; here it means splitting the salad word to let the home word in.
explanation.definitionFit: Sisters-in-law are relatives by marriage: a spouse's sisters or a sibling's wives.

clue.text: I live with cross mountain dweller

blocks.note: taken as written
to be is to exist or live
a cross is the shape of the letter X

explanation.surface: Someone admits living with a grumpy mountaineer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' reads as angry; it is the X shape.
explanation.definitionFit: The ibex is a wild goat with long curved horns found in high mountain ranges.

clue.text: Like an ale lacking head? – Composition containing hint of malt to make it smoother

definitions.note: describes the item by its purpose rather than naming it as a noun

indicators.note: lacking a head means the top is missing, so the first letter is dropped
containing means holding inside, so the trimmed word wraps around the malt letter

blocks.note: beery means like beer, of which ale is a kind
the first letter of malt, a hint of it
a paper is a written essay or composition

explanation.surface: A brewer asks how to make a flat, headless ale smoother with a little malt.
explanation.walkthrough: BEERY loses its B, then M goes after the first E. 'Head' looks like a beer's froth but means the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Emery paper is an abrasive paper rubbed on surfaces to smooth or polish them.

clue.text: Representative attends flower ceremony

blocks.note: a flower is something that flows, here the Italian river Po
a Member of Parliament represents a constituency

explanation.surface: An elected official turns up at a flower-themed ceremony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower' is the classic crossword river; the river comes first because the MP attends, or follows, it.
explanation.definitionFit: Pomp is stately display and splendour, the trappings of a formal ceremony.

clue.text: Honour Princess Hospital department? – It's well-trained

blocks.note: the OBE is a British honour, Officer of the Order of the British Empire
Diana, Princess of Wales, was known as Di
ENT is the ear, nose and throat department

explanation.surface: A query whether a hospital ward is named in honour of a princess.
explanation.definitionFit: An obedient animal or child does as told, the mark of being well-trained.

clue.text: Bank ring head of Yorkshire corporation

indicators.note: the head of a word is its opening letter

blocks.note: a pot is a kitty or pool of money, a bank in gambling
to give someone a ring is to give them a bell, British slang for a phone call
the first letter of Yorkshire

explanation.surface: A list of a Yorkshire firm's dealings: a bank, a phone call and its boss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Corporation' looks like a business; it is old British slang for a large belly.
explanation.definitionFit: Corporation is jocular dated British slang for a paunch, which a pot belly is.

clue.text: Served senior politician and top journalist

blocks.note: a government minister
the editor, abbreviated ED, heads a newspaper's journalists

explanation.surface: A list of a cabinet member's and a newspaper editor's dinner guests.
explanation.definitionFit: To minister is to attend to someone's needs, so ministered means served or tended.

clue.text: Something seen in crane's tree?

indicators.note: something seen in a phrase is sitting inside its letters, waiting to be spotted

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of crane's and the start of tree

explanation.surface: A birdwatcher asks what might be up the tree where a crane lives.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue does both jobs: the letters sit inside the phrase, and a bird's home is exactly what you would see in its tree.
explanation.definitionFit: Birds such as cranes build a nest of twigs as a home for their eggs and young.

clue.text: Cooked up strange diet including one crumble

indicators.note: something cooked up is concocted or invented, so the letters are reassembled

blocks.note: taken as written
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A cook concocts an odd diet that features a crumble pudding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strange' looks like the anagram signal but is part of the letters; 'including' adds the I to the mix. A crumble is a British baked fruit pudding, which makes the surface read as cooking.
explanation.definitionFit: To disintegrate is to break up into small pieces, which is what crumbling does.

clue.text: Refuse a stretcher

blocks.note: first meaning: rubbish dropped about, the noun refuse
second meaning: a frame for carrying a sick or injured person

explanation.walkthrough: 'Refuse' reads as the verb 'decline', but it is the noun meaning rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Litter is scattered rubbish, and also an old word for a couch or stretcher on which someone is carried.

clue.text: You start to deliver piercing smell of toilet cleaner in this pungent liquid

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter, so only that one is kept
something piercing another thing goes into it, so this pair sits inside the next word

blocks.note: the first letter of you
to rid someone of a thing is to deliver them from it
pine is the classic scent of toilet cleaners

explanation.surface: A chemist warns that the loo-cleaner whiff comes from a pungent fluid.
explanation.definitionFit: Pyridine is a foul-smelling colourless liquid used as a solvent in chemistry.

clue.text: Highlight usual placement of conductor's stand

blocks.note: first meaning: emphasise, as by drawing a line beneath words
second meaning, split in two: a music stand sits below the musical score resting on it

explanation.walkthrough: The second meaning splits the word in two: a stand goes beneath the score it holds.
explanation.definitionFit: To underscore is to emphasise, literally by underlining, so it means to highlight.

clue.text: Startling sea lions at aft of ocean wreck

indicators.note: the aft of a vessel is its rear, so only the final letter of the word is kept
a wreck is something smashed apart, so the letters are broken up and rebuilt

blocks.note: taken as written
the last letter of ocean

explanation.surface: Sea lions are startled at the stern of a wrecked ship out in the ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: Something sensational causes a sensation: it is shocking or startling news.

clue.text: Shell makes vehicle fast

blocks.note: a car is a vehicle
apace means quickly

explanation.surface: A body shell is what turns a car into a speedy machine.
explanation.definitionFit: A carapace is the hard upper shell of a tortoise, crab or similar creature.

clue.text: Bit upset and cross about magician's exit

indicators.note: upset means turned over, so in a down clue the word reads from the bottom up
about means turned around, so the word for cross is read backwards

blocks.note: a bit is a part
a rood is a cross or crucifix

explanation.surface: A conjuror's assistant is a bit upset and cross about the exit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' reads as angry; it is a rood, the old word for a crucifix.
explanation.definitionFit: A stage magician vanishes through a hinged trapdoor in the floor, so it is the conjuror's exit.

clue.text: US agents kidnap Egyptian as part of gross contract

indicators.note: kidnappers hold their victim inside, so the agents enclose the letter that follows
becoming part of something means going inside it, so this group sits within the next word

blocks.note: arrant means utter or gross, as in arrant nonsense
G-men are FBI agents, from Government men
E is the abbreviation for Egyptian, as in the Egyptian pound

explanation.surface: FBI agents snatch an Egyptian as part of a lucrative deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gross' looks like a sum of money or a dozen dozen; it is the adjective meaning utter, as in arrant nonsense. There are two nested insertions.
explanation.definitionFit: A contract is a formal agreement or deal, which is what an arrangement between parties amounts to.

clue.text: A foreign coin from long ago? Incredible!

blocks.note: un is French for a
the real was an old Spanish silver coin

explanation.surface: Someone is amazed to find an ancient coin from abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: Unreal is slang exclamation for amazing or incredible, as well as meaning not real.

clue.text: Mum entertains son's teacher

indicators.note: a host entertains guests within the home, so the mother word encloses the next letter

blocks.note: mater is a dated British word for mother
S is the abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A mother has her boy's teacher round.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is'. Mater is Latin for mother, used jokily in old-fashioned British English.
explanation.definitionFit: A master is a male schoolteacher in British usage, especially at a private school.

clue.text: Judge gets a lift when carrying pages

indicators.note: one thing carrying another holds it inside, so the lift encloses the pages

blocks.note: A plus raise, a lift in the sense of a pay rise
pp is the standard abbreviation for pages

explanation.surface: A judge is promoted while carrying a sheaf of papers.
explanation.definitionFit: To appraise is to assess or evaluate, which is what a judge does to something.

clue.text: What we're talking about is a lawyer holding information

indicators.note: holding something means having it inside, so the lawyer's letters surround the information

blocks.note: A plus DA, a US district attorney
gen is British slang for information

explanation.surface: Someone explains the meeting's topic is a lawyer with inside knowledge.
explanation.walkthrough: DA, district attorney, is the American prosecutor; the information sits between the article and the lawyer.
explanation.definitionFit: An agenda is the list of matters for discussion, so it is literally what we are talking about.

clue.text: Wear away part of guitar

blocks.note: first meaning: erode or gnaw by friction
second meaning: a raised ridge across a guitar's fingerboard

explanation.walkthrough: The first meaning is the less familiar one: besides worry, the verb means to erode.
explanation.definitionFit: Fret can mean to erode by rubbing, and is also each metal bar across the neck of a guitar.

clue.text: I love old Italian school book

blocks.note: amo is Latin for I love, Latin being the language of old Italy
S is the abbreviation for school

explanation.surface: Someone declares fondness for an old Italian school textbook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old Italian' looks like an adjective for the school; it is Latin, the language in which amo means I love.
explanation.definitionFit: Amos is a book of the Old Testament, named after the prophet.

clue.text: Trueman not playing in matches

indicators.note: playing about with letters moves them around into a fresh order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: The cricketer Fred Trueman is left out of some games.
explanation.walkthrough: Fred Trueman was a famous England fast bowler, which makes 'playing' and 'matches' read as cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: A tournament is a competition made up of a series of matches.

clue.text: Piece of wheat needed initially to make bread

indicators.note: initially points to the first letter of the word it follows

blocks.note: an ear is the grain-bearing head of a cereal plant
the first letter of needed

explanation.surface: A baker notes some wheat is required first to make a loaf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bread' is slang for money, so 'make bread' is not baking.
explanation.definitionFit: Bread is slang for money, and to earn is to make money by working.

clue.text: Coe backed narrator without initially spotting Rowling?

indicators.note: backed means put into reverse, so the name is read from right to left
initially points to the first letter of the word it follows
without here means outside, so the narrator goes around the letter

blocks.note: Sebastian Coe, the British Olympic runner, is known as Seb
a teller tells a story
the first letter of spotting

explanation.surface: Seb Coe supports a storyteller who spotted J.K. Rowling early.
explanation.walkthrough: Seb Coe is the British Olympic runner turned sports administrator. The question mark warns that Rowling is just one example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: J.K. Rowling, author of the Harry Potter books, is a prime example of a writer whose books top the sales charts.
